Gladwell's theory on what it takes to be an individual to be a leader doesn't appear in Blink, but does show what it take to be a leader, as well as how to become a leader.
"The great leaders we know were born with the right temperament and ability to form enduring relationships, and also to create things as important, if not more important than themselves" (8).
Gladwell argues that leaders are born not made. Not everything is within one's control. There are those who are born with qualities like intelligence, charisma, and tenacity.
These qualities allow them to become leaders and the rest of us can learn from their behavior (8).
For example "a child does not choose to be athletic". Instead the child has the right temperament and ability to train for success – which they do not choose (10).
"Genius can only make somebody extraordinary. It cannot necessarily make somebody a leader. Leadership is always born" (35).
The best thing you can do is to identify yourself as a leader and do the things your leader does.
In the most important leadership situations, the qualities that you had at birth would be the most helpful and the most important (8-11).
"There are very few leaders in America who have become successful because of their leadership ability" (35).
Only those who learn to lead are successful in being leaders.
All great leaders have a vision. They know where they want to go. They look ahead and think things through. They plan. Most of all they listen. They listen to people who are in the thick of things – because they know what it feels like to be part of that kind of thing (35-36).
Gladwell argues that there are five essential characteristics that separate the exceptional from the average.
Exceptional performance requires a unique set of skills and abilities (35).
"At all of the places I studied great leaders, I would always hear people saying they're a hard worker, they're motivated, and they want things done" (35).
The key question is how much effort you are willing to put into the performance.
Some people are motivated to be leaders but lack the skills to be effective.
Others, on the other hand, possess the skills but are not motivated.
Successful leaders are neither completely motivated nor completely unmotivated.
